title: King Khan Picks Christmas — and Walks Straight Into a Hollywood Ambush With Avengers, Dune and The Rock
excerpt: Shah Rukh Khan and Siddharth Anand have locked December 24 for their Pathaan reunion. The catch: Doomsday, Dune 3 and Jumanji are all crashing the same holiday week.
body:
It is the date the whole industry has been holding its breath for, and now it is official: **Shah Rukh Khan** is coming back for Christmas. *King*, his gangster-action reunion with **Siddharth Anand**, has locked **December 24, 2026** — a year-end slot that practically glows with the promise of holiday footfalls, sold-out night shows, and the kind of family-and-friends turnout the Hindi box office dreams about. SRK announced his last big swing on Pathaan's anniversary, and there is a deliciously deliberate symmetry to it: the man who rewrote his own comeback in 2023 is timing this one to the calendar's most lucrative corridor.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=M3mfut2RdHk</youtube>

And then you look at who else is in the room.

Because December 2026 is not a quiet holiday. It is a coliseum. Marvel's **Avengers: Doomsday** and Warner Bros.' **Dune: Part Three** are both staked to December 18, a week ahead. **Dwayne Johnson's** *Jumanji: Open World* lands on December 25 — the day after King. So SRK is not slipping into an empty theatre on Christmas Eve. He is muscling into a week stacked with three of the biggest franchises on the planet, all of them ravenous for the same IMAX and premium screens that King will need to make its numbers sing. For the Indian diaspora in the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf — where holiday moviegoing is a ritual and a King release is an event — this is the clash of the year before a single ticket has gone on sale.

Here is the thing, though: SRK has done exactly this before, and won.

> "#KING is Ready to ROAR on 24.12.2026 in Cinemas" — Shah Rukh Khan (@iamsrk)

The casting alone makes this a must-watch. King is mounted as SRK's most ruthless screen avatar yet — a Don, reportedly, with an emotional core threaded underneath the carnage. Beside him is his daughter **Suhana Khan**, making her big-screen debut in what may be the most scrutinised launch in modern Bollywood; the father-daughter pairing is, frankly, the most romantic marketing hook the film could ask for. Around them, an ensemble that reads like a wishlist: **Deepika Padukone** (whose involvement the makers keep coyly half-denying, which only fuels the fire), **Abhishek Bachchan**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Abhay Verma** of Munjya fame, and a rotating cast of heavyweights including Jackie Shroff, Anil Kapoor and Rani Mukerji floating through the rumour mill. This is Red Chillies Entertainment and Anand's Marflix swinging for a global event picture, not a domestic hit.

What makes the December gambit so fascinating is that it is a statement of confidence. The safe move was to dodge Hollywood entirely — slide to an early-2027 window, take a clean run at the box office, let the dust settle. The makers reportedly weighed exactly that. Instead, they planted the flag on Christmas and dared the giants to share the weekend. It is a very SRK move: the showman who has never been afraid of a stage that is too crowded, because he has always backed himself to be the one people remember walking off it.

For diaspora audiences, the practical stakes are real. Christmas week is when overseas screens fill up, when the cousins are in town, when a Hindi blockbuster can do the kind of international numbers that change a film's entire conversation. But it is also when Avengers and Dune devour the multiplex grid. The screen war in the US and Canada will be brutal, and how aggressively distributors carve out King showtimes in markets like New Jersey, the Bay Area, London and Toronto will tell you a lot about how big the trade thinks this gets.

The glimpse is reportedly coming soon, the climax is shot, post-production is the final mountain. After King, SRK is already being courted for an old-school mature romance — a sign the man is thinking in arcs again, not one-offs. But that is next year's gossip. Right now the only number that matters is 24.12.2026, circled in red on a calendar that already has three Hollywood titans scrawled across the same page. King has chosen the loudest possible room to make his entrance. The only question left is whether the crown still fits — and if you have watched this man work a holiday weekend before, you would not bet against him.
